Team Overview:
We are a two-member team consisting of Swapnil and myself, fully focused on building an innovative project for the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
We bring skills in problem-solving, technology, and research to analyze NASA data and deliver a practical, impactful solution.
(Note: Our team roster is currently complete and we are not accepting new members.)
summary:
What we developed:
We developed the SPHEREx Dual-Engine Discovery Architecture (live at www.teamprometheus.us), a zero-cost, web-based platform that transforms 102-band infrared survey data into an interactive discovery engine. It features two specialized environments: Citizen Explorer, a gamified differential blinking interface for the public, and Scientist Mode, a research console with Gaia DR3 star filtering, multi-epoch astrometry, and blackbody curve fitting.

How it addresses the challenge:
Optical telescopes fail to detect Planet X because reflected sunlight drops off exponentially over vast distances (1/r^4). Our system shifts the search to thermal infrared emission, leveraging NASA SPHEREx’s continuous 0.75–5.0 µm channels to detect the planet’s internal core heat moving against stationary background stars.

Why it is important:
It democratizes deep-space astrophysics. Running client-side with zero installation and zero server costs, it empowers anyone—from students to professional astronomers—to participate in uncovering the solar system’s next planet.
details:
Live Platform: www.teamprometheus.us

Backup platform: https://teamprometheus.diwkr7789.workers.dev
Team Members: Diwakar & Swapnil Kumar
Challenge: Planet X and SPHEREx — NASA International Space Apps Challenge 2026

MicroNotes: https://miro.com/app/board/uXjVEOZ6Vq8=/?share_link_id=815108156592

1. What Does It Do and How Does It Work?

Team Prometheus is a web-native astronomical discovery workstation engineered for NASA’s upcoming SPHEREx all-sky hyperspectral survey. Traditional optical telescopes are virtually blind to distant trans-Neptunian objects because reflected sunlight drops off exponentially by distance (1/r^4). Our platform shifts the paradigm from optical reflection to thermal infrared emission, detecting the internal heat (~40 K) radiated by an outer solar system giant across SPHEREx’s 102 continuous spectral channels (0.75 to 5.0 µm).

The platform operates through a Dual-Engine Architecture:

Citizen Explorer Mode:

  • Compresses complex 102-band data cubes into human-visible RGB composites. It automates Clyde Tombaugh’s historical blinking technique at 2 Hz, causing stationary stars to freeze while orbital proper-motion candidates (1.5–3.0 arcsec/year) visually "jump" out to the user.

Scientist Mode:

  • A full 3-column astrophysics research console featuring 6 comparison engines (Blink, Difference ΔI, Add/Stack, Swipe, Dissolve, Coadd). It cross-matches candidate coordinates with 1.8 billion stars from the ESA Gaia DR3 catalog to strip away fixed stellar foregrounds, calculates astrometric proper motion vectors, fits Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) blackbody curves, and identifies characteristic atmospheric absorption signatures (Methane at 1.66 µm/2.3 µm, Water-Ice at 3.05 µm).
  • Multi-Epoch Astronomical Comparison Engine:
  • 6 Analytical Epoch Modes: Alternates between semi-annual survey scans using Clyde Tombaugh-style Digital Blinking (150ms–1500ms cadence), Pixel Subtraction (E2 − E1 difference imaging isolating motion into dipoles), Interactive Curtain Swipe Wiping, Dual-Tone RGB Anaglyph Kinematic Vectors (Red=Epoch 1, Cyan=Epoch 2), Alpha Dissolve Cross-Fade, and 6-Detector Focal Plane Array Coaddition (boosting point-source SNR by up to 2.4× / √6).
  • Calibrated Z-Scale Histogram Stretching: Real-time Asinh non-linear contrast stretching, black/white point clipping sliders, and astronomical negative grayscale inversion for resolving faint sources against zodiacal light.
    Quantitative Analytical Tools Suite:
  • Interactive Circular Aperture Photometry: Click-to-measure flux tool that computes integrated aperture flux (MJy/sr), background sky median noise subtraction via concentric annuli (r_in to r_out), Photometric Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR), and calibrated AB apparent magnitude (m_AB) on the fly.
  • Keplerian Orbital Dynamics & Distance Solver: Applies Kepler’s Third Law (T² = a³) to candidate parallax and proper motion vectors. Users can adjust hypothesized distance (50 AU to 1,000 AU) to calculate orbital period (years), mean orbital velocity (km/s), annual reflex parallax (mas), and blackbody equilibrium surface temperature (T_eq in Kelvin), dynamically distinguishing bound trans-Neptunian objects (e.g., Planet X candidates) from high-velocity field stars.
  • Atmospheric Molecular Absorption Line Inspector: Integrates directly with the 102-band Spectral Energy Distribution (SED) engine to identify diagnostic volatile absorption band heads: Methane (CH₄ at 1.66, 2.30, and 3.30 µm), Water Ice (H₂O at 1.45, 1.95, and 3.05 µm), Carbon Dioxide (CO₂ at 4.26 µm), Carbon Monoxide (CO at 4.67 µm), and Ammonia (NH₃ at 2.00 and 2.95 µm).
  • Astrometric Distance & Angle Ruler: Vector measurement tool tracking pixel separation, angular sky separation (arcseconds), and Position Angle (PA in degrees from North through East).
  • FITS & WCS Metadata Inspector: Real-time modal inspecting IAU-standard 80-column FITS header cards (CRVAL, CRPIX, CDELT, CTYPE, TELESCOP='NASA SPHEREx', BUNIT='MJy/sr', EXPTIME) with single-click clipboard copying.
  • 2. Standardized Multi-Format Data Export
  • NASA Certified Discovery Dossier (JSON): Complete telemetry, 102-channel spectrophotometric vectors, and discovery ledger metadata.
  • IAU Minor Planet Center (MPC) 80-Column Astrometry (.txt): Standardized format ready for official orbital cataloging and Planetary Defense verification.
  • 102-Band Spectrophotometry Table (.csv): Full tabular export of channel index, wavelength, detector array assignment, flux density (µJy and MJy/sr), SNR, and spectral feature classifications.
  • Autonomous Verification Assistant: Scores signal-to-noise ratios (SNR), evaluates false-positive probability against cosmic ray artifacts, and exports publication-ready candidate dossiers.

3. What Benefits Does It Have?

  • Zero Barrier to Entry: 100% web-based. Runs immediately on any modern browser across laptops, tablets, and smartphones without software installation, Python dependencies, or account setups.
  • Solves the Historical Bottleneck: Eliminates the grueling 7,000-hour manual glass-plate inspection Clyde Tombaugh endured in 1930 to discover Pluto by automating multi-epoch diffing in real time.
  • Zero Operating Overhead: Entirely serverless and client-side rendered, eliminating costly cloud compute clusters and democratizing big-data astrophysics for classrooms worldwide.
  • High-Resilience Uptime: Features a triple-layer viewport combining live CDS Strasbourg tile streaming with guaranteed offline calibrated FITS cache fallbacks to ensure 100% visual uptime during research workflows.

4. What Is the Intended Impact?

  • Accelerating Discovery on Day One: Pre-builds the software infrastructure before NASA's SPHEREx data releases arrive, enabling immediate citizen and professional screening the moment Level-2 FITS cubes go public.
  • Democratizing Space Science: Bridges the divide between academic research and public engagement. Classrooms, amateur stargazers, and universities can collaborate on the same calibrated dataset to discover new Trans-Neptunian Objects (TNOs), brown dwarfs, and Planet X.

5. Tools, Coding Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Frontend & Rendering: HTML5, CSS3 (Awwwards-caliber glass morphic design system), Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), Canvas API, WebGL.
  • Animation & Visual Motion: GSAP (GreenSock) & ScrollTrigger, Lenis Smooth Scroll (120 FPS accelerated viewport).
  • Astrophysical APIs & Catalogs: CDS Strasbourg Aladin Lite v3 API, ESA Gaia DR3 Star Catalog, NASA IPAC / IRSA FITS standards, NASA allWISE / 2MASS multi-spectral surveys, Lowell Observatory 1930 Historical Glass Archives.
  • Data Visualization & Analytics: Chart.js (Interactive 102-channel SED spectrophotometry curves), Lucide Vector Icons.
  • Deployment & Version Control: Git, GitHub Pages, Custom DNS domain routing (teamprometheus.us), Service Worker progressive offline cache.

6. How Is Your Project Creative?

  • Cinematic Scrollytelling Experience: Replaces boring technical documentation with an interactive narrative featuring a 240-frame scroll-driven space descent, live telemetry HUDs, and ambient rocket audio.
  • The "Time Machine" Interactive Shader: An interactive comparative canvas where users scrub their cursor over Clyde Tombaugh’s original 1930 photographic discovery plate from Lowell Observatory to dynamically peel back 96 years of cosmic dust and reveal the 2026 SPHEREx infrared dipole underneath.
  • Dual-Audience Paradigm: Rather than building a dry technical tool or a superficial game, we created a unified platform where gamified citizen discovery directly feeds into research-grade astrophysical verification.

7. Factors Considered by the Team

  • Physical Constraints: Modeled the thermal blackbody emission curves for core-warmed outer planets (~40 K) and mapped them directly against SPHEREx's 6 detector arrays and filter bands.
  • Data Volume & Accessibility: Recognized that terabyte-scale hyperspectral cubes overwhelm normal home bandwidth, so we designed client-side slice streaming and range-request architectures.
  • False-Positive Mitigation: Incorporated strict astrometric criteria to differentiate true Kuiper Belt planetary motion from high proper-motion Barnard-type stars, flare stars, asteroids, and detector noise.
